subject.title: feat(gateway): watched sessions in presence with viewer facepiles

question: Should watched-session presence be limited to `operator.read` recipients through a scoped/redacted projection, or is there an intended new visibility contract for pairing and node clients?
rationale: The current behavior changes which recipients can learn session identifiers; that authorization contract cannot be chosen safely by an automated repair.

options.title: Scope watched sessions to read-authorized clients
options.body: Project watched-session data per recipient and emit only session keys that the recipient may already discover or subscribe to.

options.title: Keep presence global but omit watched sessions
options.body: Retain the existing globally visible presence shape and defer viewer facepiles until an explicit authorization-safe API is designed.

options.title: Expand recipient permissions intentionally
options.body: Document and approve a new contract that lets pairing and node clients learn watched session identifiers before retaining raw keys in global presence.

recommendation.title: Scope watched sessions to read-authorized clients
recommendation.body: Project watched-session data per recipient and emit only session keys that the recipient may already discover or subscribe to.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the identity-presence prerequisite and the current feature train, so they are the strongest available routing candidate for the intended shared-gateway visibility contract.
